title: Kasiri Ruza
dek: An archaeologist and maker whose delight in a mechanism survives difficult choices: a letter she thinks should stay undelivered, a workshop that needs partners, and an arena victory that leaves her questioning the test.

facts.Recorded at: Prima Gate; Gael coast with Severina, Thorn and Scribonia

sources: Gate chronicle · selected arrival and welcome scenes; January 2024–September 2026 posting records
Supplied character deep dives · 11 October 2026; interpretation checked against selected primary scenes where available.
body:
Kasiri Ruza wants to understand how things work, whether she is examining the Gate, fitting armor or spotting something wrong with a letter. She can be delighted by a clever construction and deeply uncomfortable when a sound deduction leaves someone else in pain. Her workshop depends on materials, hunters, customers and people willing to cooperate.

A capable maker in an empty shop

The supplied character dossier describes Kasiri as a junior partner in a Pristinian shop associated with Olokun, crediting Wren with the storefront’s construction. In its account, Kasiri sits in a dusty, mostly empty shop and identifies shortages of materials, organization and interest alongside competition. She has made a suit of plate armor to prove she can, yet that achievement has not produced a functioning supply network. The workshop’s exact name, ownership arrangement and subsequent recovery remain unconfirmed by these supplied materials.

Making something requires other people

Kasiri’s shop account distinguishes having metal and relics from having every ingredient a commission needs. Plant matter and hunted monster components can still be missing. She is candid about not yet mastering attunement-related craft and about the items she cannot make. These are limits described at that point in her development, rather than a permanent ceiling on her abilities. She seeks cooperation instead of promising work she cannot deliver.

Severina brings the field to the workshop

The dossier describes Severina as a practical counterpart: she can supply hunted components and bring demand for equipment, while Kasiri can turn those materials into durable tools. Kasiri brightens when a partnership becomes possible, jokes about unsuitable wooden or metal shoes and improvises seating when the shop has none. Her precision has warmth and embarrassment alongside it. The account supports a working relationship; it does not establish a completed contract or every proposed commission.

What Pristinia paid to shelter adventurers

In the Public Square, Kasiri tells a newcomer about flaming projectiles, damaged buildings, displaced families and Melian’s capture during the Rahu siege. She connects that memory to peace and rebuilding. When asked to condemn the Rahu collectively, she distinguishes harmful actions from a judgment against every individual. Her knowledge is informed and limited; her account is testimony, rather than a claim to know every combatant’s motives.

Primary scene: 1, 2, 3. Dates refer to Discord posts.

Craft as repayment

The supplied dossier describes Kasiri’s wish to give Pristinia more than the usual local fee: in her view, the town paid dearly to shelter adventurers when it could have blamed them. That is her assessment of a civic debt. It gives her work a purpose beyond selling equipment, while leaving the amount and completion of any additional contribution unresolved.

What remains unresolved

The supplied shop account has no message-level references or established scene date, so its details retain that provenance. Kasiri’s later mastery, the shop’s fate and the exact meaning of her occasional description of herself as a watcher remain open. Her work and her civic testimony both favor a similar discipline: use what is known, acknowledge what is missing and make cooperation possible.

Curiosity at the Gate

Kasiri approaches the activating Gate with Krasteline, eager to understand its workings. Their examination identifies ancient teleportation magic, but no discernible internal power source. Its unfamiliar runes and numerous moving parts defeat a complete reading. This limits what their investigation establishes; it does not prove the Gate has no power source.

Recognition across worlds

Kasiri introduces herself to Fenwick d’Jorasco as an archaeologist and tinkerer formerly associated with Morgrave University in Breland. She reveals a dragonmark and identifies herself with House Medani. Fenwick recognises the name; she recognises House Jorasco. Their shared recognition is an unexpected connection to home.

What remains in front of her

Kasiri tells Fenwick that, as far as she knows, nobody called here has returned. That is her knowledge at the time, not proof of a universal law. She says focusing on what is here helps her cope with missing family and friends.

The ink on Wayne’s hand

In the Common Man, Kasiri begins a morning by asking Herb for strong black coffee. An elderly woman’s distress draws her away from her cup. The company’s errand eventually takes them to Eovar for a letter from Harriett’s husband, Howard; an early misunderstanding about medicine is corrected during the quest.

When Wayne takes a conspicuously long time to find the letter, Kasiri suggests checking whether its wax is still warm. The narrator instead draws her attention to ink on his hand. She shares the clue with the others, then blushes when she realizes their suspicions are being voiced within Wayne’s hearing. His angry denial unsettles her confidence, even as she watches the others pursue the question she raised.

Wayne finally breaks down. He says that Howard died in a wreck and that, after delivering the one surviving letter, he continued writing in Howard’s name because he feared the news would kill Harriett. Kasiri asks Dex to ease off and suggests taking the conversation inside. Finding a deception has left her facing a frightened man and a decision her investigation cannot make for everyone.

A decision she stays beside

Kasiri favors sparing Harriett further anguish. She asks whether anything survived the wreck that might comfort her if they do tell her, and is told there is nothing. When Wayne seems to accept that he should confess, Kasiri points out that the group has reached no such agreement. On the road she fidgets with her gauntlets and tries to name the question plainly: should they put truth first, or Harriett’s comfort in her final days?

An encounter in the Narrows interrupts the argument. Kasiri orders Wayne behind her, then launches a bright shell from her gauntlet to mark the attackers when negotiations fail. After the fight she wants to leave before the hostility between Eovar and Pristinia brings further trouble. Her theory that the children who guided them were connected to a gang remains her deduction.

Outside Harriett’s house the company remains divided. Wayne speaks quietly to her; they embrace and go indoors. Kasiri lingers near the door, unsure whether she could help if Harriett’s condition worsens. She stays because the group has acted, even though she opposed its decision. The narrator later closes the quest with Harriett’s death that evening and her reunion with Howard’s spirit. That closing account supplies an aftermath; it is not knowledge Kasiri is shown receiving at the door.

Two woods, a forge and a willing partner

A dated scene at Jon’s forge gives a direct view of Kasiri at work with Krasteline. She carves dark and pale woods into interlocking spirals for a cane, clears her bench and adds runes and a finish. When Krasteline insists that Kasiri did the work, Kasiri answers that a partner’s success helps them both. They shake hands and hope to make more together.

The pair then decide to try armor. Kasiri buys metal and uses her own familiar tools, smiling through the heat and labor as she shapes the pieces. Krasteline helps and encourages her. Kasiri carries the cooling pieces with her gauntlets and drains her waterskin when the work is done. Their conversation records pride in what they have made; it does not settle every later crafting ruling, ownership arrangement or commission in the separate shop account.

Questions with too few answers

At the Oíche Arena, Kasiri is immediately distracted by Kumai’s construction. She asks about the warforged’s unfamiliar design before remembering the question put to her. She says she has concentrated on improving her skills for the common cause, rather than fighting other adventurers. Soon she offers her magical, martial and crafting talents to the proposed vanguard.

Kumai’s tests make that assurance harder to sustain. In a hypothetical battlefield choice she favors the battalion over a beloved companion or a relic. Asked about an alliance built around a concealed traitor, she complains that the scenario excludes possible negotiations before answering within its terms. The threatened condemnation of a fallen friend’s soul visibly shakes her. These are answers to an examiner’s constructed choices, not sacrifices she actually carries out.

When asked whom she would follow, Kasiri names Severina, whom she trusts even at a cost to herself. She also values Modeli’s compassion and reluctance to waste a life. Severina in turn argues that Kasiri could make different talents work together. The choices expose their different grounds for trust; Kumai’s eventual request for further discussion leaves the leadership question open at the end of this session.

Winning, and still objecting

The practical test becomes a fight among the candidates and Kumai. Kasiri trades blows and spells with familiar companions, congratulates Modeli’s spell even as it hurts, and tries to turn her frustration at his evasions into encouragement. Boots, protective runes, gauntlets and stubbornly effective magical darts all find a use. Eventually the contest comes down to her and Thorn.

Kasiri wins by wearing the druid down, then lowers herself to the arena floor exhausted. The narrator records the participants revived afterward. She offers Thorn a hand and admires the unfamiliar pillars that nearly beat her. Her victory brings no sudden reverence for the test: she wants to know why Kumai set inflexible moral problems, joined the fight himself and then sent them away to choose a leader.

Severina tries to calm her. Kasiri accepts that the argument can wait, and returns to the Common Man with her thoughts. The maker who said direct competition was not her priority has won the bout, but winning has not answered her questions about how it was run.

From the shop to the mist

When mist stops outside Pristinia during the Acolyte attack, Kasiri arrives from her shop with newly made boots and checks her armor’s runes. Camilla warns against casting in the mist; Kasiri immediately asks whether a spell already active outside it could be carried in. Camilla says that has not been tested. The attack begins before Kasiri can try her experiment.

She runs to keep up with Severina’s horse, uses her gauntlets in the fighting and presses on after being knocked down. Once the mist retreats, she is uneasy at how abruptly it ends and extends her sight to look for more. The company has beaten back this attack; the taunting voice’s claim of much greater strength remains a threat, and Kasiri has no proof that the next danger is gone.

The things she means to preserve

Walking with Severina on the Gael coast, Kasiri meets Scribonia. When he asks why they fight, she answers as a craftswoman: she makes things, and understands Death as seeking their end. Her participation does not come from particular devotion to Cala or Nuru. She also remembers having been pulled here without consent.

The conversation turns to Thorn’s hopes for groves and connected islands. Scribonia warns that a goal without firm limits can be exploited. Kasiri challenges his method rather than his opposition to annihilation. Harsh experience already comes from the monsters, she says; allies need some softness too.

Scribonia defends blunt confrontation and admits that he does not understand people as they do. Kasiri is not persuaded that an intended lesson excuses how it is delivered. She leaves with Severina, asking what victory would mean if nothing comfortable or gentle remained. The scene gives her position its own voice; it does not settle their disagreement.

profile.relationships: Recognizes Fenwick through their shared home-world institutions. A forge scene directly records partnership with Krasteline; the separate shop dossier names Olokun and credits Wren’s storefront. Severina supplies materials, earns Kasiri’s trust and calms her after the vanguard trial. Kasiri helps Thorn up after their final bout.
profile.personality: Curious, practical and capable of excitement, embarrassment and exasperation. Finding a deception does not make its moral consequences easy for her. She can win a contest and still object to the way it was run; her civic testimony resists condemning every Rahu individual.
profile.achievements: Investigates the Gate and welcomes Fenwick, pursues the clue in Wayne’s letter, works wood and armor with Krasteline, seeks materials and customers for a struggling shop, wins the vanguard trial’s bout and joins the defense against Acolyte. The shop’s exact arrangement and later fate retain their earlier uncertainty.
